headline_marked: Bangladesh [[requests extradition of ex-Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal]] from India
headline: Bangladesh requests extradition of ex-Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal from India
summary: Bangladesh has formally requested India to extradite former Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, who was sentenced to death for crimes against humanity during the July-August mass uprising. The verdict copy has also been sent.
details: Bangladesh has formally requested the Indian government to extradite former Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal. He was sentenced to death for crimes against humanity committed during the July-August mass uprising.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs recently sent a letter to the Indian government seeking Kamal's return. Along with the request, a copy of the International Crimes Tribunal's death sentence verdict against him was also forwarded.
Kamal was accused alongside Sheikh Hasina and former IGP Chowdhury Abdullah Al-Mamun in a case filed over crimes against humanity during the 2024 July-August mass uprising.

Following judicial proceedings, International Crimes Tribunal-1 delivered its verdict on November 17, 2025. The tribunal sentenced both Sheikh Hasina and Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal to death for crimes against humanity. Former IGP Chowdhury Abdullah Al-Mamun, who was a state witness in the same case, received a five-year prison sentence.
caption:
Bangladesh has formally requested India to extradite former Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal. He faces a death sentence for crimes against humanity.

Bangladesh has formally requested the Indian government to extradite former Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal. He was sentenced to death for crimes against humanity committed during the July-August mass uprising.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs recently sent a letter to the Indian government seeking Kamal's return. Along with the request, a copy of the International Crimes Tribunal's death sentence verdict against him was also forwarded.

Kamal was accused alongside Sheikh Hasina and former IGP Chowdhury Abdullah Al-Mamun in a case filed over crimes against humanity during the 2024 July-August mass uprising.

Following judicial proceedings, International Crimes Tribunal-1 delivered its verdict on November 17, 2025. The tribunal sentenced both Sheikh Hasina and Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal to death for crimes against humanity. Former IGP Chowdhury Abdullah Al-Mamun, who was a state witness in the same case, received a five-year prison sentence.
